60:1: Abu Ja`far said: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from among the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, O you who have believed, do not take My enemies from among the polytheists and your enemies as allies meaning supporters. And His statement, You extend to them affection, He, the Most High, says: You extend to them your affection for them. The inclusion of the ba in His statement, with affection, and its omission are the same, similar to the saying of the speaker: I want you to go and I want you to go, the same, and like His statement, And whoever intends therein to commit injustice (al-Hajj 22:25), and the meaning is: And whoever intends therein to commit injustice and wrong. And from that is the saying of the poet: When she wanted to drink, he shook the stick at her, leaning forward. Meaning: When I wanted to drink. And they have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth. He says: These polytheists whom I forbade you to take as allies have disbelieved in what has come to you of the truth from God, and that is their disbelief in God, His Messenger, and His Book that He revealed to His Messenger. And His statement, They will expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord, God Almighty says: They will expel the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and you, meaning: And they will also expel you from your homes and your land, and that is the expulsion of the polytheists of Quraysh of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions from Mecca. And His saying: That you believe in God, your Lord, God Almighty says: They will expel the Messenger and you from your homes because you believed in God. And His statement: If you have gone forth to strive in My cause and seeking My pleasure is from the deferred which means to bring forward, and the point of the speech is: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection while they have disbelieved in what came to you of the truth. If you have gone forth to strive in My cause and seeking My pleasure, they will expel the Messenger and you because you believe in God, your Lord. And what He, the Most High, means by His statement: If you have gone forth to strive in My cause is: if you have left your homes and migrated from them to your place of migration to strive in My way which I have prescribed for you and My religion which I have commanded you to follow and to seek My pleasure. And His statement, And you conceal your affection towards them, means that the Most High says to the believing companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: You conceal your affection towards the polytheists, O believers. And I know what you conceal, meaning: I know better than you what some of you conceal from one another, and what you declare. And what you declare, meaning: I also know better than you what some of you declare to one another. And whoever among you does it has certainly strayed from the right path, meaning: He, the Most High, says: And whoever among you conceals his affection towards the polytheists, O believers, has certainly strayed from the right path, which God has made a path to Paradise and a way to it. It was mentioned that these verses from the beginning of this Surah were revealed concerning Hatib bin Abi Balta’ah, who had written to the Quraysh in Mecca informing them of a matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had hidden from them. This is what came in the reports and narrations from a group of the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and others. Who said that? Ubayd ibn Ismail al-Hibari and al-Fudayl ibn al-Sabah told me: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Ali, who told me: Ubayd God ibn Abi Rafi’ said: I heard Ali, may God be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent me, al-Zubayr ibn al-Awwam, and al-Miqdad. Al-Fadl said: Sufyan said: A group of the emigrants, and he said: Go until you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set off, our horses racing with us until we reached the garden, and we found a woman. We said: Bring out the letter. She said: I do not have a letter. We said: Either you bring out the letter, or we will throw away the clothes. So she took it out from her tie, and we took the letter and went with it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. In it was from Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah to some people in Mecca, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O Hatib, what is this? He said: O Messenger of God, do not rush me. I was a matter attached to the Quraysh, and I had no kinship with them. Those of the Muhajireen who were with you had kinship, and they protected their families in Mecca. So I wanted, since I missed that in terms of kinship, to take a hand in it with which they would protect my kinship. I did not do that out of disbelief or apostasy from my religion, nor was I satisfied with disbelief after Islam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: He has told you the truth. Umar said: O Messenger of God, let me strike off the head of this hypocrite. He said: He witnessed Badr, and how do you know? Perhaps God looked at the people of Badr and said: Do what you want, for I have forgiven you. Al-Fadl added to his hadith. Sufyan said: And the verse was revealed concerning him: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies until His saying: until you believe in God alone. Ibn Humayd narrated: Mihran narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Sinan Sa`id ibn Sinan, on the authority of `Amr ibn Murrah al-Jamali, on the authority of Abu al-Bukhtari al-Ta`i, on the authority of al-Harith, on the authority of `Ali may God be pleased with him, who said: When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) wanted to go to Mecca, he confided in some of his companions that he intended to go to Mecca, among them Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah. He spread the word among the people that he intended to go to Khaybar, so Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah wrote to the people of Mecca that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) intended to go to you. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent me and Abu Marthad, and there was not a man among us who did not have a horse. He said: Go to Rawdat Khakh, for you will find a woman there with a letter, so take it from her. So we set out until we saw her in the place that the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had mentioned, and we said: Give me the letter. She said: I do not have a letter with me. So we put down her belongings and searched, but we did not find it among her belongings. Abu Marthad said: Perhaps it is not with her. I said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) did not lie, nor did he lie. So we said: Bring out the letter, or we will strip you naked. Amr ibn Murrah said: So she brought it out from her pocket. Habib said: She brought it out from her side. We brought it to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and there was a letter from Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah to the people of Makkah. Umar said: He has betrayed God and His Messenger. Allow me to strike off his head. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Did he not participate in Badr? He said: Yes, but he broke his oath and supported your enemies against you. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Perhaps God has looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you want. Umar’s eyes welled up and he said: God and His Messenger know best. So he sent for Hatib and said: What made you do what you did? He said: O Prophet of God, I was a man attached to the Quraysh, and I had family and wealth there, and there was not one of your companions who did not have someone in Mecca who would protect his family and wealth, so I wrote to them about that. By God, O Prophet of God, I believe in God and His Messenger. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah has spoken the truth, so do not say anything about Hatib except good. Habib ibn Abi Thabit said, then God Almighty revealed: O you who have believed, do not take My enemy and your enemy the verse. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told us, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, that his statement, O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, extending to them affection to the end of the verse was revealed about a man from the Quraysh who was with the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, in Medina. He wrote to his family and clan in Mecca, informing them and warning them that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was going to them. He informed the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, of his document, so he sent `Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, to it, and he brought it to him. Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ja`far ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of `Urwah ibn al-Zubayr and other scholars of ours, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, decided to march to Mecca, Hatib ibn Abi Balta`ah wrote a letter to the Quraysh informing them of the matter that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had decided to march against them. Then he gave him a woman whom Muhammad ibn Ja`far claimed was from Muzaynah, and others claimed was Sarah, a slave girl of some of the Banu `Abd al-Muttalib. He gave her a reward so that she would convey it to the Quraysh. She put it in her hair, then twisted her hair around it, then she went out. report of what Hatib had done came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky. So he sent `Ali ibn Abi Talib and al-Zubayr ibn al-`Awwam, may God be pleased with them both, and said: Catch up with a woman with whom Hatib had written a letter to the Quraysh, warning them of what we have agreed to do with them. So they went out until they caught up with her at al-Hulaifah, al-Hulaifah ibn Abi Ahmad. They brought her down and searched in her saddlebags, but they did not find her. Something, so Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, said to her: I swear by God that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not lie, nor did we. You must bring me this letter, or we will expose you. When she saw his seriousness, she said: Turn away from me. So he turned away from her, so she untied the horns of her head, and she took out the letter and gave it to him. He brought it to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, called Hatib and said: O Hatib, what made you do this? He said: O Messenger of God, by God, I am a believer in God and His Messenger. I have not changed or altered anything, but I was a man among the people who had no origin or clan, and I had family and children among them, so I treated them kindly regarding him. Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, said: Leave me, O Messenger of God, so that I may strike off his head, for the man has been a hypocrite. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: How do you know, O Umar? Perhaps God looked at the companions of Badr on the day of Badr and said: Do what you will, for I have forgiven you. Then God, the Almighty, revealed about Hatib: O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies until His saying: And to you we have turned until the end of the story. Ibn Abd al-A'la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Urwah, who said: When the verse, O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies was revealed about Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah, he wrote a letter to the infidels of Quraysh advising them. God informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of that, so he sent Ali and al-Zubayr and said: Go, for you will find a woman in such and such a place. So they brought a letter with her and set out until they caught up with her. They said: The letter that you have with you! She said: I do not have a letter. They said: By God, we will not leave anything with you without searching it or bringing it out. She said: Are you not Muslims? They said: "Yes, but the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, told us that you have a letter and we are certain that you have it." When she saw their seriousness, she took out a letter from between her horns and took it to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, and it was written: From Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah to the infidels of Quraysh. The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, called him and said: Did you write this letter? He said: Yes. He said: What made you do that? He said: By God, I have never doubted God since I became a Muslim, but I was a stranger among you, O tribe of Quraysh, and I had wealth and children in Mecca, so I wanted to defend them with that. Umar may God be pleased with him said: Give me permission, O Messenger of God, to strike off his head. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Take it easy, O son of Al-Khattab. How do you know? Perhaps God has looked at the people of Badr and said: Do whatever you want, for I am forgiving you. Al-Zuhri said: The verse Forgiving, Most Merciful was revealed about him. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, Do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies to His statement, He is Seeing of what you do, in the correspondence of Hatib ibn Abi Balta’ah and those with him to the infidels of Quraysh, warning them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, do not take My enemies and your enemies as allies, until he reached the straight path. He mentioned to us that Hatib wrote to the people of Mecca informing them of the Prophet’s march to them at the time of Hudaybiyyah. God, the Almighty, informed His Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, of that, and mentioned to us that they found the letter with a woman in a horn of her head. The Prophet of God, peace and blessings be upon him, called him and said, What made you do what you did? He said, “By God, I did not doubt God’s command, nor did I renounce it, but I had family and wealth there, so I wanted to make peace with the Quraysh regarding my family and wealth.” He mentioned to us that he was an ally of the Quraysh but was not one of them. Then God, the Almighty, revealed the Qur’an regarding that, and said, If they gain the upper hand over you, they will be enemies to you and stretch out their hands and tongues against you with evil, and they would like you to disbelieve.
60:2: God Almighty says: If these people, to whom you confide your love, should seize you, O believers, they will become enemies and warlords to you, and they will stretch out their hands against you in fighting and their tongues in evil. His statement: And they wish that you would disbelieve means: They wish that you would disbelieve in your Lord, so that you would be like them.
60:3: And His statement: Never will your wombs, nor your children, benefit you on the Day of Resurrection. God Almighty says: Do not let your wombs, relatives, and children call you to disbelieve in God and take His enemies as allies, extending love to them. For neither your wombs, nor your children will benefit you with God on the Day of Resurrection, nor will they ward off God's punishment from you on that Day, if you disobeyed Him in this world and disbelieved in Him. And His saying: He will judge between you, God Almighty says: Your Lord, O believers, will judge between you on the Day of Resurrection by admitting those who obey Him into Paradise, and those who disobey and disbelieve in Him into Hell. The reciters differed in their recitation of this. The majority of the reciters of Medina, Mecca, and Basra recited it yufasil baynakum with a damma on the ya’ and a soft and fatha on the sad, as long as the agent was not named. The majority of the reciters of Kufa, except for Asim, recited it with a damma on the ya’ and a shaddah on the sad and a kasrah, meaning: God separates between you, O people. Asim recited it with a fatha on the ya’ and a soft and kasrah on the sad, meaning God separates between you. Some of the reciters of Ash-Sham recited yufasil with a damma on the ya’ and a fatha and shaddah on the sad as long as the agent was not named. These readings are close in meaning and correct in grammar, so whichever one the reader reads, he is correct. And His statement: And God is Seeing of what you do, meaning that God Almighty says: God, O people, is All-Knowing and All-Seeing of your deeds. Nothing of them is hidden from Him. He encompasses them all, and He will reward you for them: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. So fear God in yourselves and beware of Him.
60:4: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: There has certainly been for you, O believers, an excellent example. He says: A good example in Abraham, the friend of the Most Merciful, for you to follow his example, and those with him from the prophets of God. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding the words of God Almighty, There has certainly been for you a good example in Abraham and those with him, he said: Those with him are the prophets. And His statement: When they said to their people, ‘Indeed, we are innocent of you and of whatever you worship besides God,’ meaning: When they said to their people who disbelieved in God and worshipped the tyrant: O people, indeed we are innocent of you and of whatever you worship besides God of gods and rivals. And His statement: We have disbelieved in you, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever until you believe in God alone. God Almighty is saying, informing about what His prophets said to their disbelieving al-Nas 114:We have disbelieved in you, we have denied what you were upon of disbelief in God, and we have denied that your worship of what you worship besides God is true, and there has appeared between us and you enmity and hatred forever because of your disbelief in God and your worship of what is other than Him. There will be no peace between us nor truce until you believe in God alone. He says: until you believe in God alone, make Him One, and single Him out for worship. And His statement: Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ but I have no power over you against God at all. God Almighty says: You have a good example in Abraham and those with him in these matters that we have mentioned of his opposition to the disbelievers and his enmity towards them, and his abandonment of friendship with them, except in Abraham’s saying to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you. For you have no example in him in that, because that was from God Almighty to his father regarding a promise He had made to him before it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God. So when it became clear to him that he was an enemy of God, he disavowed him. God Almighty says: So too you, O believers in God, disavow the enemies of God among those who associate others with Him, and do not take them as allies until they believe in God alone and disavow the worship of anything other than Him and show them enmity and hatred. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Except for the saying of Abraham to his father, he said: They were forbidden to follow the example of Abraham’s seeking forgiveness for his father, and to seek forgiveness for the polytheists. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Abu Ja`far, on the authority of Mutraf al-Harithi, on the authority of Mujahid, A good example in Abraham until His saying, I will surely ask forgiveness for you. He said: In everything he did there was an example, except asking forgiveness for his father. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, There has certainly been for you a good example in Abraham, follow his example in everything except his statement to his father, I will surely ask forgiveness for you, so do not follow his example in that, for it was because of a promise he had made to him. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Except for the statement of Abraham to his father, he said: Do not be sad about that, for it was an appointment made for him, and be sad about all of his affairs. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God Almighty, There has certainly been for you a good example, to His statement, except for the statement of Abraham to his father, ‘I will surely ask forgiveness for you,’ he said: He says: You have no example in this. What he means by his saying: And I have no power over anything for you against God is: And I have no power over anything for you against God’s punishment if God punished you for your disbelief in Him, and I cannot protect you from it in any way. And His statement, Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, is that He, the Most High, is informing us of what Abraham and his prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, said: Our Lord, in You we have put our trust, and to You we have turned, meaning: and to You we have returned in repentance from what You dislike for what You love and are pleased with. And to You is the final destination, meaning: and to You is our final destination and our return on the day You raise us from our graves and gather us on the Day of Resurrection to the place of presentation.
60:5: God Almighty says, informing us of what Abraham, His friend, and those with him said: “O our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieved in You, denied Your Oneness, and worshipped other than You, by giving them power over us, so that they see that they are right and I am wrong, and thus make us a trial for them.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Husayn told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, he said: Do not punish us by their hands, nor by a punishment from You, lest they say: If these people had been on the truth, this would not have happened to them. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Our Lord, do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, he said: He says: Do not make them prevail over us, lest they be tempted by that, and see that they have only prevailed over us because of a right they have over us. Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, Do not make us a trial for those who disbelieve, meaning: Do not give them power over us so that they tempt us. And His saying: And forgive us, our Lord means: And cover our sins for us by pardoning us for them, O our Lord. Indeed, You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise meaning the One who is severe in taking revenge on whoever takes revenge on him. The Wise: He says the Wise in His management of His creation, and His directing them toward what is best for them.
60:6: And His statement: There has certainly been for you in them an excellent pattern means that God Almighty says: “There has certainly been for you, O believers, an excellent pattern in those mentioned by Abraham and those with him of the prophets, may God’s prayers be upon them, and the messengers, “for whoever hopes in God and the Last Day” means: whoever among you hopes to meet God, and God’s reward, and salvation on the Last Day. And His statement, And whoever turns away - then indeed, God is the Free of need, the Praiseworthy. God Almighty says: And whoever turns away from what God has commanded him to do and urged him to do, from among you and others, and turns away from it and turns away arrogantly, and befriends the enemies of God, and expresses love towards them - then indeed, God is the One who is free from his faith in Him, his obedience to Him, and from all of His creation. He is Praiseworthy with the people of knowledge for His favors and blessings upon them.
60:7: God Almighty says: Perhaps God will, O believers, establish love between you and those of My enemies from among the polytheists of Quraysh with whom you are hostile. So God did that with them, as many of them converted to Islam and became their allies and parties. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, Perhaps God will establish affection between you and those of them with whom you are at enmity, he said: These polytheists He has done so, He has brought them into peace and established affection between them when Islam was at the time of the conquest. And His statement, And God is All-Powerful, means: God has the ability to establish affection between you and those polytheists with whom you are hostile. And God is Forgiving and Merciful, means: God is Forgiving of the sins of those who show affection to the polytheists if they repent from them, and Merciful to them that He does not punish them after they repent from them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, “Perhaps God will establish affection between you and those among you with whom you are at enmity. And God is competent to do that.” And God is Forgiving and Merciful. He forgives many sins and is Merciful to His servants.
60:8: God Almighty says, God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion of the people of Mecca and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them meaning, and being just toward them by being kind to them and being righteous toward them. The commentators differed about who was meant by this verse. Some of them said that it meant those who believed in Mecca but did not emigrate, so God gave permission to the believers to be kind to them and treat them well. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Amr told us, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion that you ask forgiveness for them, and be righteous toward them and act justly toward them, he said: They are those who believed in Mecca and did not emigrate. Others said: It means those who did not emigrate from outside Mecca. Who said that? Muhammad bin Ibrahim Al-Anmati told me: Harun bin Maruf told us: Bishr bin Al-Sarri told us: Mus`ab bin Thabit told us, on the authority of his uncle, `Amir bin `Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, who said: This was revealed concerning Asma’ bint Abi Bakr. They had a mother in the pre-Islamic period called Qutaylah bint `Abd Al-`Uzza. She brought her gifts, a jug of dates, dried yogurt, and butter. She said: I will not accept any gift from you, and do not enter upon me until the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) gives permission. `Aishah mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), and God revealed: God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion until His saying: those who are just. He said: Ibrahim bin Al-Hajjaj told us, he said: Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak told us, he said: Mus`ab bin Thabit told us, on the authority of `Amir bin Abdullah bin Al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, he said: Qatilah bint `Abd Al-`Uzza bin Sa`d from Banu Malik bin Hasal came to visit her daughter Asma bint Abi Bakr, and he mentioned something similar. Others said: Rather, what he meant by it were the polytheists of Mecca who did not fight the believers, nor did they expel them from their homes. He said: And God abrogated that later with the command to fight them. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the statement of God Almighty: God does not forbid you, so he said: This has been abrogated. Fighting abrogated it. They were ordered to return to them with swords, and to fight them with them, to strike them, and God set for them a deadline of four months, either slaughter or Islam. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, God does not forbid you, he said: It was abrogated by Kill the polytheists wherever you find them (al-Tawbah 9:5). The most correct of the sayings on this matter is the saying of the one who said: What is meant by that is, God does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion, from all kinds of religions and faiths, from being good to them, connecting with them, and being just to them, because God Almighty included in His saying those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes all those who are like that, so He did not specify some over others. And there is no meaning to the saying of the one who said: That is abrogated, because the believer’s kindness to those who are at war with him, those who are related to him by blood, or those who are not related to him or have no blood relationship, is not forbidden and is not prohibited if there is no indication in that for him or for the people at war of the vulnerability of the people of Islam, or to strengthen them with a leg or weapon. The correctness of what we said on that matter has been demonstrated by the report that we mentioned on the authority of Ibn al-Zubayr in the story of Asma and her mother. His saying, God loves those who are just, means that God loves those who are just and who treat people fairly, give them their rights and justice, are righteous to those who are righteous to them, and are good to those who are good to them.
60:9: God Almighty says: “God only forbids you, O believers, from those who fight you because of religion, from among the disbelievers of Mecca, and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion, from making friends with them.” He says: And aid those who expelled you from your homes in expelling you, from making friends with them, so that you will be their allies and supporters. And whoever makes them allies, He says: And whoever makes them allies from among you or from others, then it is those who are the wrongdoers. He says: So it is those who made friends with other than those whom they are permitted to make friends with, and placed their allies in the wrong place, and disobeyed God’s command in that. And similar to what we said about the meaning of His statement, those who fought you because of religion, the people of interpretation said. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid: God only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion. He said: The infidels of the people of Mecca.
60:10: God Almighty says to the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants from the land of disbelief to the land of Islam, examine them. And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, examined them when they came as emigrants: Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus bin Bakir narrated to us, on the authority of Qais bin Ar-Rabi’, on the authority of Al-Aghar bin Al-Sabah, on the authority of Khalifa bin Husayn, on the authority of Abu Nasr Al-Asadi, who said: Ibn Abbas was asked: How did the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, test the women? He said: He would test them by God, as long as they left out of hatred for their husbands, and by God, as long as they left out of desire for one land to another, and by God, as long as they left out of worldly gain, and by God, as long as they left out of love for God and His Messenger. Abu Kuraib told us: Al-Hasan bin Atiyah told us, on the authority of Qais, who said: Al-Aghar bin Al-Sabah told us, on the authority of Khalifa bin Husayn, on the authority of Abu Nasr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. He said: When a woman came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, he would make her swear by God that she would not go out, then he mentioned something similar. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that Aisha said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not test the believing women except with the verse. God said, When believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, and no, no. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Wahb told us: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab: Urwah ibn al-Zubayr told me that Aisha, the wife of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: When the believing women migrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, they were tested by the words of God: O Prophet, when the believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you to the end of the verse. Aisha said: Whoever among the believing women acknowledges this has acknowledged love. So when the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, acknowledged this in their words, he would say to them: Go, for I have given you my allegiance. By God, the hand of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never touched the hand of a woman, except that he gave them his allegiance verbally. Aisha said: By God, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, never took a pledge from the women except by what God Almighty commanded him to do. And he would say to them when he took a pledge from them: I have given you my allegiance verbally. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants to His statement, All-Knowing, All-Wise, their test was to testify that there is no god but God, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Ibn Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, Then examine them, he said: Ask them what brought them about. If what brought them about was anger at their husbands, or his displeasure, or something else, and he did not believe, then return them to their husbands. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada: Then test them. Their test was that they would be succeeded by God. What drove you out was disobedience, and what drove you out was nothing but love for Islam and its people, and eagerness for it. So if they said that, he would accept it from them. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, Then examine them, he said: They swear that they did not go out except out of a desire for Islam and love for God and His Messenger. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of his father or Ikrimah, If believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. He said: It is said: Nothing brought you except the love of God, nor did it bring you the love of a man from among us, nor did it bring you fleeing from your husband. So that is what His saying examine them means. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said: When a woman from among the polytheists became angry with her husband, and there was a conversation between them, she would say: By God, I will migrate to Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions. So God Almighty said: When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. If she was brought on by anger, then reject her, but if she was brought on by Islam, then do not reject her. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Bakir ibn al-Ashja, he said: Their test was that nothing made you leave except religion. His saying, God knows best about their faith, means: God knows best about the faith of the women who came to you as immigrants. And His statement, And if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers, means: If they acknowledge during the trial what would make the contract of faith for them and their entry into Islam valid, then do not return them to the disbelievers at that time. This was only said to the believers because the covenant had been made between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists of Quraysh in the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah that the Muslims would return to the polytheists whoever came to them as Muslims. So that condition was nullified for the women if they came as believing emigrants and were tested, and the Muslims found them to be believers, and this was valid for them from what we mentioned before. And they were commanded not to return them to the polytheists if they were known to be believers. And God, Most High, said to them, “And if you know them to be believers, do not return them to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for them, nor are they lawful for them,” meaning: Neither are the believing women lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for the believing women. The traces came in a similar manner to what we said. Mentioning some of what was narrated in this regard: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, saying: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: I entered upon Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, while he was writing a letter to Ibn Abi Hunayd, the companion of al-Walid ibn Abd al-Malik. He wrote to him asking him about the words of God, the Exalted, When believing women come to you as emigrants until His words, And God is Knowing and Wise. Urwah ibn al-Zubayr wrote to him: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a treaty with the Quraysh in the year of al-Hudaybiyyah on the condition that he would return to them whoever came without the permission of his guardian. But when the women emigrated to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to Islam, God refused to return them to the polytheists when they were tested by the ordeal of Islam, and they knew that they had only come out of a desire for it. And His saying, And give them what they spent, God Almighty says: And give to the polytheists whose women came to you as believers, if you know them to be believers and you have not returned them to them, what they spent in marrying them as a dowry. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, to His statement, All-Knowing, All-Wise, he said: Their test was that they should testify that there is no god but God and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger. Then, if they knew that this was true of them, they would not return them to the disbelievers, and her husband, one of the disbelievers for whom the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) had made a contract, would be given the dowry that he had given her. Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And give them what they spent and give their husbands their dowries. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding His statement, “O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them. God knows best about their faith,” until he reached, And God is Knowing and Wise. This is a ruling that God, the Exalted, the Majestic, has made between the people of guidance and the people of misguidance. If you flee from the polytheists who had a treaty with the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and his companions, then marry them, and send their dowries to their husbands from the polytheists who had a treaty with the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). And if you flee from the Companions of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to the polytheists who had a treaty with the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), then send their dowries to their husbands from the Companions of the Prophet of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: It was revealed to him while he was at the foot of al-Hudaybiyyah. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made peace with them, that whoever came to him from among them he would return them to them. When the women came to him, this verse was revealed to him, and he was commanded to return the dowry to their husbands. He ruled similarly for the polytheists: if a Muslim woman came to them, they should return the dowry to their husbands. He said: And do not hold on to the ties of marriage of disbelieving women. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Mu’adh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, “Then test them. God knows best as to their faith.” The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made a treaty with the polytheists and the People of the Book. He made a treaty with them and they made a treaty with him. One of the conditions was that they should return the wealth and women. So when the Prophet of God missed one of the wives of the believers and she joined the treaty, abandoning her religion and choosing polytheism, he would return and ask her, What brought you out from your people? If he found her leaving seeking Islam, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would accept her and return to her husband what he had spent on her. But if he found her fleeing from her husband to another with whom she was related, and she was clinging to polytheism, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would return her to her husband from among the polytheists. Yunus ibn Abd al-A’la told me, saying: Ibn Wahb told us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement, O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them and the entire verse, he said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, made a truce with the polytheists, one of the conditions he stipulated was that you should return to us whoever comes to you from us, and we will return to you whoever comes to us from you. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, Whoever comes to us from you, we will return him to you, and whoever comes to you from us and chooses disbelief over belief, we have no need of them. He said: But God refused that for the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and did not pay attention to the men, so God, the Exalted, said, When believing women come to you as emigrants, examine them until His statement, and give them what they spent their husbands. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Amr ibn al-Harith told me, on the authority of Bakir ibn al-Ashja, he said: There was a truce between the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the polytheists regarding the women who had fled. So if a polytheist woman fled, the Muslims would give her husband his support, and the Muslims would do the same. And if these people were not given the support, the Muslims would give the Muslim whose wife had fled her support. And His statement, And there is no blame upon you if you marry them if you have given them their dowries, God Almighty says: “And there is no blame upon you, O believers, if you marry these emigrant women who have joined you from the land of war, separated from their husbands, even if they have husbands in the land of war, if you know them to be believers, then you have given them their dowries.” By dowries, he means the charity. Qatada used to say: “All of them, if they fled from the polytheists who had a treaty with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, and his companions, and they married them, they sent their dowries to their husbands from the polytheists who had a treaty with the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Bishr told us that, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada. Al-Zuhri used to say: God only ordered that their dowries be returned to them if they were withheld from them, if they returned to the Muslims the dowries of the women they had withheld from them. Ibn Hamid told us that. He said: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Zuhri. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, “And there is no blame upon you if you marry them,” and she has a husband then, because Islam separated them, if they have purified their wombs. And His saying, And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women, God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: Do not hold on, O believers, to the ropes and ties of disbelieving women. Disbelieving women is the plural of disbeliever, and bonds are the plural of bond, which is what one holds on to from the knot and the ties. This is a prohibition from God to the believers from proceeding to marry polytheistic women from the people of idols, and He commands them to separate from them. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yaqub ibn Ibrahim told me: Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us: `Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us: Mu`ammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of `Urwah, on the authority of al-Miswar ibn Makhrama and Marwan ibn al-Hakam, that believing women came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, after he had written the treaty between him and the Quraysh. Then God revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, until He reached: By the protection of the disbelieving women. So `Umar divorced on that day two of his wives who had been his partners in polytheism, and he married one of them, Mu`awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan, and the other, Safwan ibn Umayya. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, he said: Rather, we know that the verse of the trial in which the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) extended the time of the infidels of Quraysh was because of the treaty that was between the infidels of Quraysh and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) would return to the infidels of Quraysh what they spent on their women who converted to Islam and emigrated while their husbands were infidels, because of the treaty that was between the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and them. If they had been at war and there was no period or contract between them and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), he would not have returned to them anything of what they spent. God ruled for the believers over the people of the treaty from the infidels in a similar manner. God said: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you as emigrants, until He reached: And God is Knowing and Wise. So the believers divorced every infidel woman who was married to a man from among them when this verse was revealed. Umar ibn al-Khattab may God be pleased with him divorced his wife, the daughter of Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughira from Banu Makhzum, and Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her, and the daughter of Jarwal from Khuza’ah. Abu Jahm married her from the cleverness of Al-Adawi, and God made that a ruling by which he ruled between the believers and the polytheists during this period that was. Ibn Humayd told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, who said: Al-Zuhri said: When this verse was revealed: O you who have believed, when believing women come to you until His saying: And do not hold fast to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women, among those whom Umar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, divorced was the daughter of Abu Umayyah ibn al-Mughira, and Muawiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married her after him, while they were still polytheists in Mecca. Umm Kulthum, the daughter of Jarwal al-Khuza’iyyah, the mother of Abdullah ibn Umar, and Abu Jahm ibn Hudhaqah ibn Ghanim, a man from his people, married her, while they were still polytheists. Talhah ibn Ubayd God ibn Uthman ibn Amr al-Taymi had Arwa bint Rabi’ah ibn al-Harith ibn Abd al-Muttalib with him, and Islam separated them when the Qur’an forbade holding fast to the marriage bonds of disbelieving women. Talhah had migrated while she was in Mecca following the religion of her people, and then Khalid ibn Sa’id ibn al-‘As ibn Umayyah ibn Abd Shams married her in Islam after Talhah. He was among those who fled to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from… The women of the infidels who had no covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he imprisoned her and married her to a Muslim man, Umaimah bint Bishr al-Ansariyyah, then one of the women of Banu Umayyah ibn Zayd from Aws God, she was married to Thabit ibn al-Dahdaha, so she fled from him while he was a disbeliever to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, married her to Sahl ibn Hunaif, one of Banu Amr ibn Awf, and she gave birth to Abdullah ibn Sahl. Ibn Abd al-A’la told me: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, that God said: And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women. Al-Zuhri said: So Umar divorced two of his wives in Mecca. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, And do not hold on to the bonds of disbelieving women. He said: The companions of Muhammad were ordered to divorce their disbelieving wives in Mecca, so they stayed with the disbelievers. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, And do not hold on to the bonds of the disbelieving women, referring to the polytheistic Arab women who refused Islam. He ordered that they be set free. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His statement, And do not hold on to the ties of disbelieving women, if a woman disbelieves, do not hold on to her, leave her alone. Separation occurred between her and her husband when she disbelieved. The reciters differed in their recitation of His statement, And do not hold on. The majority of the reciters of the Hijaz, Medina, Kufa, and the Levant read it as And do not hold on with a light seen. Abu Amr read it as And do not hold on with a heavy seen. He mentioned that it was the recitation of Al-Hasan, and he considered whoever read it with a light seen, and holding on is known. The correct thing to say about this is that they are two well-known readings and two famous languages, narrated from the Arabs, which I have held on to and held on to. And His statement, And ask what you have spent, and let them ask what they have spent, says the Almighty to the wives of those believers who joined the polytheists in Mecca from the disbelievers of Quraysh, “And ask, O believers whose wives have gone and joined the polytheists, what you spent on your wives who joined them of dowry from those whom you married from among them, and let the polytheists among them whose wives joined you as believers ask you, when they married from among you, what they spent on them of dowry.” And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Yunus told me: He said: Ibn Wahb told us: He said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: The believers acknowledged God’s ruling and paid what they were commanded to do regarding the expenses of the polytheists that they spent on their women, and the polytheists refused to acknowledge God’s ruling regarding what He imposed upon them regarding paying the expenses of the Muslims. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God, And ask what you have spent, and let them ask what they have spent, he said: Whatever wives of the Companions of Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, went to the infidels, let the infidels give them their dowries and let them keep them. And whatever wives of the infidels went to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, the same applies to the peace treaty that was between Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Quraysh. And His statement, That is the judgment of God, He judges between you, God Almighty says: This is the judgment that I have judged between you, O believers, regarding your affair with the polytheists, regarding what you spent on your wives who joined them, and He ordered them to ask you the same regarding their wives who joined you. It is God’s judgment between you, so do not transgress it, for the truth is that which no one else hears. So the believers from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, referred to God’s command and judgment, and the polytheists refused it and demanded that the conditions that they had stipulated between them in that peace treaty be fulfilled. And this is what came in the reports and narrations from the people of biography and others. The narration mentioned that: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: As for the believers, they acknowledged God’s ruling, but as for the polytheists, they refused to acknowledge it, so God Almighty revealed: And if any of your wives have escaped you to the disbelievers, the verse. Ibn Humayd narrated to us: Salamah narrated to us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Az-Zuhri, who said: God said: That is the judgment of God; He judges between you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, kept the women and returned the men, and asked the one whom God had commanded to ask from the dowries of the women whom they had kept back, and to return to them the same as they return to them if they did so. And were it not for the judgment that God had decreed, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would have returned the women, just as he returned the men. And were it not for the truce and treaty that was between him and the Quraysh on the day of Al-Hudaybiyyah, he would have kept the women and not returned their dowries. And this is what He does with those Muslim women who came to him before the treaty. His statement: And God is Knowing and Wise means, may His praise be exalted: God is All-Knowing and All-Wise in His management of them.
60:11: God Almighty says to the believing companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, And if you, O believers, have lost any of your wives to the disbelievers, then he will join them. The interpreters of the Quran differed regarding the unbelievers meant by His statement, to the unbelievers. Who are they? Some of them said: They are the unbelievers who had no covenant with the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. They said: The meaning of the statement is: And if you miss any of your wives, to those with whom you have no covenant from the unbelievers. Who said that? Muhammad bin Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding His statement, And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, those with whom there is no covenant. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, And if any of your wives escape to the disbelievers if they fled from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to disbelievers between whom and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, there was no covenant. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib bin Abi Thabit, on the authority of Mujahid: And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, he said: There was no covenant between them. Others said: Rather, they are the infidels of Quraysh who were people of a truce, and this is what Al-Zuhri said. Yunus told me this. He said: Ibn Wahb told us. He said: Yunus told me on his authority. And his saying, So you punished: The reciters differed in their recitation of that, so the majority of the reciters of the regions read it as So you punished with an alif, on the example of Fa’altum, meaning: you inflicted a consequence on them. And Hamid al-A’raj read it, as was mentioned from him, as So you punished with the example of Fa’altum, with a doubled qaf. And they are in the difference of wording with them similar to his saying, And do not turn your cheek away from people (Luqman 31:18), and turning away despite the closeness of their meanings. Abu Jaafar said: The more correct of the two readings in my opinion is the reading of the one who read it fa’aqabtum with an alif, due to the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it. His statement, Then give those whose wives have gone to the unbelievers the equivalent of what they spent on them as a dowry, means: Give those among you whose wives have gone to the unbelievers the equivalent of what they spent on them as a dowry. The commentators differed regarding the money that he was ordered to give to the one whose wife had gone to the polytheists. Some of them said: They were ordered to give them the dowry of the polytheist women who had joined them. Who said that? Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Yunus told me, on the authority of Al-Zuhri, he said: The believers acknowledged the ruling of God and paid what they were commanded to pay of the expenses of the polytheists that they spent on their wives, and the polytheists refused to acknowledge the ruling of God regarding what He imposed upon them regarding paying the expenses of the Muslims, so God said to the believers: “And if any of your wives have gone to the disbelievers and you have punished them, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they spent. And fear God, in whom you are believers.” So if, after this verse, a woman from the wives of the believers were to go to the polytheists, the believers would return to her husband the expenses that he spent on her from the heirs that they had in their hands, which they were commanded to return to the polytheists from their expenses that they spent on their wives who believed and emigrated, then they would return to the polytheists any surplus if it remained for them, and the heirs are what was in the hands of the believers from the dowries of the women of the disbelievers when they believed and emigrated. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: God revealed, And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers and you have punished them, then give those whose wives have passed away an equivalent to what they spent. So God commanded the believers to return the dowry if a Muslim woman passes away and she has a husband, that the Muslims return to him the dowry of his wife from the dowry if it is in their hands from what they were commanded to return to the polytheists. Others said: Rather, they were ordered to give him from the spoils or the booty. Muhammad ibn Sa`d told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn `Abbas, regarding his statement, “And if any of your wives have gone to the disbelievers and you have punished them, then give those whose wives have gone away an equivalent to what they spent. And fear God, in whom you are believers,” meaning: If the wife of a man from the Muhajireen joins the disbelievers, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, commanded that he be given from the spoils an equivalent to what he spent. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, that they were ordered to return to them some of the spoils, and Mujahid used to recite So you punished. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us both, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, Then you punished he says: you took spoils from Quraysh or others, then give those whose wives have gone the equivalent of what they spent their dowries in exchange. Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi Thabit, on the authority of Mujahid: And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers he said: If there was no treaty between them and a woman who went to the polytheists, then her husband should be given a dowry similar to hers and you punished and obtained booty then give those whose wives have passed away the equivalent of what they spent and fear God he said: A dowry similar to hers should be given to her husband. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, And if any of your wives have gone to the disbelievers and you have punished them, then give those whose wives have gone away an equivalent of what they spent and fear God, when the companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fled to the disbelievers, there was no covenant between them and the Prophet of God, and the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took spoils, her husband would be given what he brought to her from all the spoils, then they would divide their spoils. Ahmad bin Yusuf told me, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: I heard Al-Kisa’i narrating on the authority of Za’idah, on the authority of Al-A’mash, on the authority of Muslim, on the authority of Masruq, that he read it as So you punished and interpreted it as So you gained. Ahmad told us, he said: Al-Qasim told us, he said: Hisham told us, on the authority of Mughira, on the authority of Ibrahim, regarding his statement, Then you punished, he said: You gained booty. Ibn Hamid told us: Salamah told us, on the authority of Ibn Ishaq, who said: We asked Al-Zuhri about this verse and the statement of God, And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, he said: He says: If any of you has passed away to the disbelievers, and no woman comes to you, for whom you can take the same as what they take from you, then compensate her from the spoils of war if you obtain it. Others said about this: Yunus narrated to me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said regarding His statement, And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, and you have punished [her], he said: A woman from among the people of Islam went out to the polytheists, and no one else went out. He said: Then a woman from among the polytheists came, and the people said: This is your punishment that has come to you. So God said, And if any of your wives have passed away to the disbelievers, and you have punished [her], meaning: You have kept what came to you from them because of what you have with them. Then give those whose wives have passed away the equivalent of what they spent. Then God informed them that there is no blame on them if they do what they did if they marry them after her womb is purified. He said: So the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) called the one whose wife had gone to the disbelievers, and he said to the one who had come from the polytheists: This is the husband of the one who went away. Should I marry him to you? She said: O Messenger of God, God has excused this wife of his if she runs away from him. No, by God, I have no need of him. So the Bukhtari called a large man and said: This one? She said: Weeping, and she was one of those who had come from Mecca. The most correct of the sayings on this matter is to say: God Almighty commanded the believers in this verse to give to the wife of a believer whose wife fled to the unbelievers if they had a consequence against the unbelievers, either by way of spoils that they obtain from them, or by having the women of some of them join them, like what they spent on the one who fled from them to them. He did not specify that they be given that from money rather than money, so they must give them that from all the money that we mentioned. And His statement: And fear God, in whom you believe, means: And fear God, in whom you believe, O believers, so fear Him by performing His obligations and avoiding His sins.
60:12: God Almighty says to His Prophet Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: “O Prophet, when believing women come to you pledging allegiance to you that they will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill their children, nor bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet.” He says: Nor will they bring forth a lie they have fabricated about a child born between their hands and feet. The meaning of the statement is: And they will not attribute to their husbands anyone other than their children. And the people of interpretation said something similar to what we said about that. Who said that? Ali told me, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And let them not bring forth a slander which they have invented between their hands and their feet, meaning: No one shall be attributed to their husbands except their children. His saying: And they will not disobey you in anything good, means: And they will not disobey you, O Muhammad, in anything good that God Almighty commands them to do. And he mentioned that the good thing in which he stipulated that they not disobey the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is wailing. Who said that? Ali told us, he said: Abu Saleh told us, he said: Muawiyah told us, on the authority of Ali, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, his statement, And they do not disobey you in what is right, meaning: they do not bow down. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abd al-Rahman told us, he said: Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, And they do not disobey you in what is right, he said: wailing. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Abu Ahmad told us, he said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim bin Abi Al-Jaad, the same. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansour, on the authority of Salim, the same. Muhammad bin Ubaid Al-Maharbi told us: Musa bin Umair told us, on the authority of Abu Salih, regarding his statement, And they do not disobey you in what is right, he said: in wailing. Ibn Hamid told us, he said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Salim ibn Abi al-Ja`d, And they do not disobey you in what is right. He said: Wailing. He said: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, And they do not disobey you in what is right. He said: They do not scratch their faces, nor tear their clothes, nor cry out in grief, nor recite poetry. Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, he said: The trial of the women was that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, ordered Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, and said: Tell them: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, asks you to pledge allegiance that you will not associate anything with God. Hind bint Utbah bin Rabi’ah, who split open the belly of Hamza, may God have mercy on him, was disguised among the women, and she said: I will not speak so that he may recognize me, and if he recognizes me, he will kill me. I only disguised myself out of fear of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. The women who were with Hind remained silent and refused to speak. Hind said, disguised,: How can he accept from women something that he does not accept from men? The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) looked at her and said to Umar, Tell them not to steal. Hind said, By God, I sometimes commit sins against Abu Sufyan, and I do not know whether they are permissible for me or not. Abu Sufyan said, Whatever I have committed, whether in the past or in the future, is permissible for you. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) laughed and recognized her. He called her and she came to him, took his hand and sought refuge with him. He said, Are you Hind? She said, God has pardoned what is past. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) turned away from her and said, nor should they commit adultery. She said, O Messenger of God, does a free woman commit adultery? He said, No, by God, a free woman does not commit adultery. He said, nor should they kill their children. Hind said, You killed them on the Day of Badr, and you and they are more aware. He said, nor should they bring forth a slander they have invented between their hands and feet, nor should they disobey you in what is right. He said, He forbade them from wailing. The people of the Age of Ignorance used to tear their clothes, scratch their faces, cut their hair, and call for destruction and woe.” Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, O Prophet, when the believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you, until he reached, then pledge allegiance to them. He mentioned to us, “That the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from them on that day the obligation of wailing, and not to speak to men, except to a man among you who is a mahram. Then Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said, O Prophet of God, we have guests, and we are absent from our women.” He said, “The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘I did not mean those.’” Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, And let them not disobey you in what is right. He said: It is wailing. He ordered them not to wail, and not to be alone with men except in the presence of a mahram. He said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf said: We are absent and we have guests. He said: That is not what I meant. Ibn Bashar told us, he said: Sulayman told us, he said: Abu Hilal told us, he said: Qatada told us, regarding His statement, And let them not disobey you in what is right, he said: Let them not tell a man. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Ayyash told me, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Amr ibn Shu`ayb, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, he said: “Umaymah bint Ruqayqah came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge allegiance to him on Islam. The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to her: ‘I pledge allegiance to you on the condition that you will not associate anything with God, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill your child, will not fabricate a lie between your hands and feet, will not wail, and will not display your beauty in the manner of the first days of ignorance.’” Ibn Hamid told us: Mihran told us, on the authority of Sufyan, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqayqah, who said: Women came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, to pledge allegiance to him. He said: As much as they can. And they were released and said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves. Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Abdul-Hakam narrated: My father and Shuaib ibn al-Layth narrated to us, on the authority of al-Layth, who narrated to us Khalid ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Hilal, on the authority of Ibn al-Munkadir: Umaimah informed him that she entered upon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with some women, and they said: O Messenger of God, extend your hand so that we may shake hands with you. He said: I do not shake hands with women, but I will take a covenant with you. So he took a covenant with us until he reached: And let them not disobey you in what is right. Then he said: In what you have given freedom and are able to do. They said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves. Ibn Hamid told us: Harun told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Ibn Sirin, on the authority of Umm Atiyyah al-Ansariyyah, who said: Among the conditions stipulated for us regarding kindness when we pledged allegiance was that we would not wail. A woman from the Banu so-and-so tribe said: The Banu so-and-so tribe made me happy, so I will not repay them until I repay them. So she went and made them happy, then she came and pledged allegiance. He said: None of them fulfilled their promise except her and Umm Sulaym bint Milhan, the mother of Anas ibn Malik. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Abu Nu`aym narrated to us, saying: Amr ibn Farukh al-Qattat narrated to us, saying: Mus`ab ibn Nuh al-Ansari narrated to us, saying: I met an old woman of ours who was among those who pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. She said: So I came to him to pledge allegiance to him, but he took from us something and did not bow. Then an old woman said: O Prophet of God, some people had made me happy when misfortunes had befallen me, and now a misfortune has befallen them, so I want to make them happy. He said: Then go and reward them. Then she came and he pledged allegiance to him. He said: It is the good thing about which God said: And let them not disobey you in what is right. Abu Kurayb told us: We were told by Wakee’, on the authority of Yazid, the freed slave of Al-Sahba’, on the authority of Shahr bin Hawshab, on the authority of Umm Salamah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding his statement, And they do not disobey you in what is right, he said: Wailing. Abu Kurayb narrated to us, saying: Yunus narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqaiqah al-Taymiyyah, who said: I pledged allegiance to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, along with some Muslim women. We said to him: We have come to you, O Messenger of God, to pledge allegiance to you that we will not associate anything with God, nor steal, nor commit adultery, nor kill our children, nor fabricate a lie between our hands and feet, nor disobey you in what is right. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: To the best of our ability and capacity. We said: God and His Messenger are more merciful to us than we are to ourselves. We said: Give us allegiance, O Messenger of God. He said: Go, for I have pledged allegiance to you. My words to one hundred women are like my words to one woman, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not shake hands with any of us. Abu Kurayb told us: Yunus bin Bakir told us, on the authority of Isa bin Abdullah al-Tamimi, on the authority of Muhammad bin al-Munkadir, on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqayqah, the aunt of Fatimah, the daughter of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: I heard her say: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, pledged allegiance to us, and he made a covenant with us that we would not associate anything with God, and he mentioned a hadith similar to that of Muhammad bin Ishaq.
