Muhammad ibn Bashar narrated to us, he said: Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, he said: Sufyan narrated to us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqayqah, she said: I came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, with some women to pledge allegiance to him. She said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, took from us what is in the Qur’an: That you should not associate anything with God. Then he said: As much as you are able to do. So we said: O Messenger of God, will you not shake hands with us? He said: “I do not shake hands with women. My words to one woman are like my words to a hundred women.” Ibn Abd al-Rahim al-Barqi told us: Amr ibn Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Zuhair, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, on the authority of Umaimah bint Ruqayqah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, in a similar manner. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Hussein, who said: I heard Abu Muadh, who said: Ubaid narrated to us, who said: I heard Al-Dahhak say regarding His statement, And they do not disobey you in what is right, and what is right is what He stipulated for them in the pledge of allegiance, that they follow his command. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, And let them not disobey you in what is right, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, is His Prophet and the best of His creation, and he did not make lawful for him any of the matters he commanded except with a condition. He did not say and let them not disobey you and leave it until he said in what is right. So how should anyone be obeyed in what is not right when God stipulated this for His Prophet? He said: He commanded them to do what is right in all matters, and they should not disobey. “Muhammad ibn Sinan al-Qazzaz narrated to us, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Idris, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Uthman ibn Ya’qub, on the authority of Ismail ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Atiyah, on the authority of his grandmother Umm Atiyah, who said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he gathered the women of the Ansar in a house. Then he sent for us ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab, who stood at the door and greeted us. We responded, or we responded to him. Then he said: ‘I am the messenger of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to you.’ We said: ‘Welcome to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and to the Messenger of the Messenger of God.’ He said: ‘Will you pledge allegiance that you will not associate anything with God, will not steal, and will not commit adultery?’ She said: ‘We said: Yes.’ He extended his hand from outside the door or the house, and we extended our hands from inside the house. Then he said: ‘O God, bear witness!’ She said: ‘And he ordered us to go out on the two Eids, menstruating women and young women, and that there was no Friday prayer for us, and he forbade us from following funeral processions.’ Ismail said: ‘So I asked my grandmother about the statement of God, ‘And they will not disobey you in what is right. ’ She said: ‘Lamentation.. Muhammad bin Abdul Rahim Al-Barqi told me: Omar bin Abi Salamah told us, on the authority of Zuhair, regarding the statement of God, “And they do not disobey you in what is right,” he said: A man should not be alone with a woman. And His statement, Then take their pledge of allegiance, God Almighty says: If the believing women come to you to pledge allegiance to you on these conditions, then take their pledge of allegiance. And ask forgiveness for them from God, meaning: Ask God to forgive them their sins and conceal them by His pardoning them for them. Indeed, God is Forgiving and Merciful, meaning: God is the One who conceals the sins of whoever repents to Him from his sins, lest He punish him for them after he has repented from them.
60:13: God Almighty says to the believers in Him from the companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace: O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry from the Jews. They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves. The commentators differed in their interpretation of His statement, They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves. Some of them said: The meaning of this is: These people, upon whom God was angry, from the Jews, have despaired of God’s reward in the Hereafter, and of being resurrected, just as the living have despaired of their dead who are in the graves returning to them. Who said that? Muhammad bin Saad told me, he said: My father told me, he said: My uncle told me, he said: My father told me, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding his statement, O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry, meaning those who have died among those who disbelieved, for the living among those who disbelieved have despaired of ever returning to them, or of God resurrecting them. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us: Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur bin Zadhan, on the authority of Al-Husayn, that he said regarding this verse, They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves. He said: The living disbelievers have despaired of the dead. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatada, regarding his statement, They have despaired of the Hereafter, he said: They have despaired of being resurrected, just as the disbelievers despaired of the return of the dead to their graves. Bishr told us, he said: Yazid told us, he said: Saeed told us, on the authority of Qatada, his statement, O you who have believed, do not take as allies those with whom God has become angry and who have despaired of the Hereafter, the disbeliever does not hope to meet his dead or his reward. It was narrated on the authority of Al-Husayn, who said: I heard Abu Muadh say: Ubayd narrated to us, who said: I heard Ad-Dahhak say regarding His statement, They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves, he said: Whoever dies from among those who disbelieve, the living among them have despaired of returning to them, or of God resurrecting them. Others said: Rather, the meaning of this is that they have despaired of God having mercy on them in the Hereafter and forgiving them, just as the unbelievers who are in graves and have died and gone to their graves have despaired of God’s mercy and forgiveness for them in the Hereafter, because they have become certain of God’s punishment for them. Who said that? Ibn Al-Muthanna told us: Muhammad bin Ja`far told us, on the authority of Al-Hakam, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding this verse, They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves. He said: The inhabitants of the graves, those in the graves, have despaired of the Hereafter. Muhammad ibn Amr told me, he said: Abu Asim told us, he said: Isa told us, and Al-Harith told me, he said: Al-Hasan told us, he said: Warqa’ told us, both of them, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding his statement, They have despaired of the Hereafter, just as the disbelievers have despaired of the inhabitants of the graves, he said: Of the reward of the Hereafter when their deeds become clear to them, and they see the Fire. Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, he said: Muhammad told us, he said: Shu’bah told us, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, that he said regarding this verse, They have despaired of the Hereafter, he said: The people of the graves have despaired of the Hereafter. Ibn Abd al-A’la told us: Ibn Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, who said: Al-Kalbi said: They have despaired of the Hereafter, meaning the Jews and Christians. He said: They have despaired of the reward and honor of the Hereafter, just as the unbelievers who have died and are in their graves despaired of Paradise when they saw their place in Hell. Yunus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb told us, he said: Ibn Zayd said, regarding the statement of God, Do not take as allies a people, he said: These disbelievers have despaired of ever having an afterlife, just as the disbelievers who died and are in the graves have despaired of ever having an afterlife, when they witnessed the matter of the afterlife. So just as those disbelievers despaired, so too have these disbelievers despaired. He said: The people upon whom God became angry are their Jews, who have despaired of ever having an afterlife, just as the disbelievers before them despaired of the people of the graves, because they had learned the Book of God and persisted in disbelief in it, and they did not do it, although they knew. Ibn Hamid told us: Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, regarding his statement, They despair of the Hereafter, he said: They have despaired of ever having the reward of the Hereafter, just as the unbelievers in their graves despaired of good when they saw the torment and humiliation. The more correct of the two opinions on this matter, in my opinion, is the opinion of the one who said: These Jews, upon whom God became angry, have despaired of God’s reward for them in the Hereafter, and of His honor for their disbelief and denial of His Messenger Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, even though they knew that he was a prophet of God, just as the disbelievers among them who passed away before them despaired and perished, and became the people of the graves, and they are in the same state as these people are in their denial of Jesus, may God bless him and grant him peace, and other messengers, of God’s reward and honor for them. We said: This is the more correct of the two interpretations of the verse, because the dead have despaired of returning to the world, or of being resurrected before the Hour comes, both the believers and the disbelievers. So there is no reason to limit this report to the disbelievers, and the believers have shared in their despair of that.
